executive_summary.narrative: The assessment revealed a broad attack surface with multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, though many were not fully proven due to time constraints and require further verification. The immediate priority should be addressing the SQL injection and XSS issues (W-002, W-003, W-004, W-009) as they can lead to data compromise. For the unproven findings, treat them as hypotheses and conduct targeted retesting as part of remediation. Confidence in these results is moderate; the untested findings (W-011 through W-015) are based on code review and configuration analysis, so verify them with automated tools or manual testing. Prioritize fixes that are low effort and high impact, such as securing unauth endpoints and adding rate limiting, to quickly reduce risk.

findings.status: tested, not proven (signal 'error' did not appear in the response)
findings.recommendation: For /rest/user/login, parameterize all SQL queries or use an ORM that prevents SQL injection. Implement prepared statements with parameter binding for the login query, and sanitize user input. Also, consider using a stored procedure if direct queries are necessary.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to /rest/admin may expose admin functions
findings.recommendation: Restrict /rest/admin to authenticated users with an 'admin' role. Add a security filter or middleware that checks the user's role and denies access otherwise. Remove any hard-coded credentials or backdoors that might allow anonymous access.

findings.title: Information disclosure in /rest/admin/application-configuration
findings.recommendation: Secure /rest/admin/application-configuration by requiring authentication and authorization. This endpoint should only be accessible to administrators, and sensitive configuration data should be redacted or not returned at all. Use fine-grained access controls.

findings.status: tested, not proven (HTTP 500: an error page is not evidence of this flaw)

findings.title: Mass assignment on /register or /api/Users
findings.recommendation: For /register, implement a whitelist of allowed fields for user creation. Ignore any extra parameters in the request, and explicitly assign only expected fields like username, email, and password. Do not allow setting roles or other privileged attributes via mass assignment.

findings.recommendation: Add rate limiting to /rest/user/login to prevent brute force attacks. Use a tool like Fail2ban or implement custom middleware to limit login attempts per IP and per user, with a lockout after several failed attempts.

caveats: Produced by an autonomous pipeline with no human review. Findings should be validated by a security engineer before remediation is prioritised or the results are shared externally.
API routes were extracted from client-side JavaScript. They are candidate routes the application references, not a verified inventory of its endpoints.
15 of 15 findings were not proven exploitable (W-002, W-003, W-015, W-008, W-009, W-005, W-001, W-006, …). They are hypotheses based on observed assets, not demonstrated vulnerabilities.
5 findings were never tested for exploitability (W-011, W-012, W-013, W-014, W-015). No claim is made about them either way.
Absence of a finding is not evidence of absence. This engagement covered what the crawler reached within its configured bounds.
